examples.name: Default
examples.summary: A relative range (`Last 15 minutes`) that stays relative: the value is `{ type: 'relative', amount, unit }`, re-resolved against the clock on every query. The panel has two tabs, Relative and Absolute, and opens on Relative here because the value is relative (an absolute or `since` value opens Absolute). Relative lists the quick ranges with a blue **Custom range** link right under them that opens a duration and unit form in their place (Back to quick ranges returns). Absolute opens on the month grid, only as many weeks as the month needs, with Month and Year selects between the arrows to jump far back; the blue **Enter dates** link swaps the grid for the Start and End date and time fields (typed, or picked from a 30-minute list), and **Show calendar** swaps back. **End at now** works in both views. Refresh every sits in the footer beside Cancel and Apply (`↻ 5 min`, on by default), so the page handles `@refresh` by re-running its query. The panel is as thin as the calendar and commits nothing until Apply; the page states the time zone next to the picker (see the Events explorer block). Unset, `min` is five years ago and `max` the end of today. On a phone it opens as a full-width sheet from the bottom of the screen.

examples.name: Absolute
examples.summary: `range-selector-mode="absolute-only"` with a `max`: the month grid first, and **Enter dates** for the typed date and time fields. The trigger prints the range in the zone with its UTC offset, and Apply refuses an end before the start or past the limit with an inline message.

examples.name: RelativeOnly
examples.summary: `range-selector-mode="relative-only"` with the default quick ranges (Today to Last year) and the blue Custom range link under them, for a metrics interval that is always measured back from now.

examples.name: WithStep
examples.summary: `show-step` adds Previous and Next around the trigger; each moves the range by its own length (an hour back, an hour forward) and Next stops at the present. A range inside one day prints its date once (`Nov 10, 13:00 – 14:00`), and the trigger text wraps instead of being cut off when the space is narrow.

examples.name: UntilNow
examples.summary: An absolute start that ends now: tick **End at now** on the Absolute tab, under the calendar or under the typed fields, and the value becomes `{ type: 'since', start }` (the calendar then picks only the start day). The trigger reads `Nov 10, 2026, 9:30 – now`, the end moves with the clock on every query, and Next stays disabled.

examples.name: AutoRefresh
examples.summary: Refresh every sits in the panel footer beside Cancel and Apply (`↻ 1 min`) and is on by default at 5 minutes (Off, 10 sec … 1 hr); this page starts it at 1 minute. Bind `v-model:refresh-interval` (seconds, 0 is off) and run the query on `@refresh`, which fires on each tick while the page is visible; the trigger draws no refresh icon and says the interval to screen readers. A page that cannot re-run its query passes `:show-refresh="false"`. The quick ranges start with **Today** and **This week**: options with `snap: true` begin at the start of the day or week in the time zone.

examples.name: TimeZone
examples.summary: `v-model:time-zone` and `show-time-zone` with a short list of zones: the panel shows the zone selector, the absolute range is typed and shown in the chosen zone, and the stored value stays the same ISO instants, printed under the picker. Without `show-time-zone` the panel says nothing about the zone; the page shows it beside the picker.

examples.name: Limits
examples.summary: `:max-duration="{ amount: 90, unit: 'day' }"` caps the range at 90 days with the default bounds (five years back to the end of today): Last year leaves the quick ranges, a longer custom duration or calendar range is refused with `Choose a range of 90 days or less.`, and once a start day is picked the days more than 90 days away are disabled.

examples.name: FutureDates
examples.summary: A maintenance window in the future: `max` a year ahead lifts the default end-of-today limit, `min` stops the past, and `max-duration` of one day keeps the window short. Use the same `max` for token expiry or an alert schedule.

examples.name: Disabled
examples.summary: A disabled picker keeps its range visible; the trigger and the step buttons do not respond.
